Rice University advertises its endowed professorship in Jain Studies

The Tirthankar Shantinath Professorship in Houston is open at assistant level, with associate level and tenure possible for qualified candidates. Materials should arrive by 15 November 2026 for fullest consideration.

Talaash Heritage desk · Published 6 November 2026

Where
Houston, Texas, USA
Apply by
15 November 2026

Rice University in Houston, Texas, is seeking a scholar for the Tirthankar Shantinath Professorship in Jain Studies, in its School of Humanities and Arts. The post is advertised at assistant professor level, and a qualified candidate may be appointed as an associate professor with tenure. The appointee must be eligible for a post in one of the school's departments.

The research areas the university lists, any one or more of which may apply, are applied Jainism, bioethics or medical humanities, and South Asian culture, religion, philosophy or history. The holder should know the textual languages well enough to teach courses on Jainism and supervise advanced research, though the search committee will also consider specialists in bioethics, science or medical practice.

The holder is expected to help shape applied Jainism, a young field that brings ahimsa (non-violence), aparigraha (non-possessiveness) and anekantavada (pluralism) to bear on the humanities. The advertisement describes the chair as supported by a significant endowment and as a chance to set up an interdisciplinary programme.

Candidates must hold a PhD in Jain Studies, South Asian Studies or a related field by 1 July 2027, the day the appointment begins. The teaching load is two courses each semester.

Applications go through Interfolio and need a cover letter, CV, research statement with five-year plan, statement of teaching philosophy and interests, a sample syllabus for an undergraduate elective, a writing sample of up to 25 pages and three letters of recommendation. Review has already begun and will continue until the post is filled, but materials should be in by 15 November 2026 for fullest consideration.
